## Goal

**User story:** As a balance engineer, I want tests that pin how scaled enemy counts reach the campaign (static and sequenced) without breaking determinism or the existing campaign invariants, so the density change cannot silently reshape the authored campaign.

Test-first item for the parent AC "Enemy counts rise with level" (AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P).

## What to do

Add tests (in the existing wave test files, or a new `src/waves/scaledCampaign.test.ts`) that:

- Assert level-1 `LEVELS` wave groups are unchanged by the scaling path (deep-equal counts), so onboarding data stays byte-identical.
- Assert a level-10 group grows by the documented multiplier with the documented rounding, floor of 1, 200-per-group cap, and `single`-formation groups remain exactly 1.
- Assert the scaling is applied to **both** the static `LEVELS` campaign and the sequenced campaign (`buildSequencedLevels`, covering `fixed`, `curve` and `dynamic` generation modes), through the shared build seam.
- Assert same-seed builds remain byte-identical (determinism contract) and that a second build of the same campaign is idempotent (no double scaling).
- Assert the scaled campaign still satisfies the existing invariants and wave-balance rules: `campaignInvariants.test.ts`, `campaignRoster.test.ts`, `waveBalance` R1–R3, `campaignBalanceAudit.test.ts`.
- Assert the shared helper is the only scaling implementation consumed by game and gym launch paths (parity seam), not a duplicated copy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New tests fail on pre-change HEAD for the specified reason (no scaling applied/nonexistent helper).
- Tests cover level-1 identity, level-10 growth, rounding, floor, cap, `single` groups, both campaign paths, same-seed determinism and no double scaling.
- Tests cover scaled-campaign compliance with the existing campaign invariants and wave-balance rules.
- No production code is modified by this item (tests only).

**Key Files:**

- `src/waves/Formations.test.ts`, `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`
- optionally `src/waves/scaledCampaign.test.ts` (new)
- existing invariant suites: `src/waves/campaignInvariants.test.ts`, `src/core/waveBalance.test.ts`

## Dependencies

Blocked by: "Add level-scaling module and tunable rules" (needs the helper contract). Blocks the campaign count-application feature.

## Goal

**User story:** As a balance engineer, I want deterministic tests that prove the kill-time power-up supply falls with the campaign level, so the supply curve cannot regress unnoticed.

Test-first item for the parent AC "Power-up supply per enemy falls with level" (AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P).

## What to do

Extend `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` (and the rules tests where appropriate) with tests that:

- Force the scene RNG so the number of drops over N kills is exact and deterministic at level 1 (matches the current 0.18 rate) and at level 10 (matches 0.05, i.e. at most 30 % of the level-1 rate).
- Prove the level is resolved from the live campaign (`WaveManager.currentLevel()?.level`), i.e. after advancing a level the next kills use the new chance, and an unknown level falls back to level 1.
- Prove the small-asteroid Extra Life roll scales by the same ratio and is unchanged at level 1 (`rules.asteroidExtraLifeDropChance`).
- Prove drop types/weights, the mineral kill-drop rule and timed weapon/power-up effects are unaffected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New tests fail on pre-change HEAD (flat 0.18 roll for every level).
- Assertions are exact and seeded — no statistical/threshold flakiness.
- Coverage includes level 1 identity, level 10 endpoint, mid-run level advance, unknown-level fallback and Extra Life proportionality.
- No production code is modified by this item (tests only).

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`
- `src/core/rules.test.ts`

## Dependencies

Blocked by: "Add level-scaling module and tunable rules". Blocks the PlayScene drop-roll feature.

# Mining laser

## Problem statement

Asteroids are an inert world hazard that drift through the field and drop minerals when destroyed (small asteroids drop one mineral; a large chain is 1 + 2 + 4 = 7 destroys). Mining them competes directly with shooting the actual threats, so mineral farming is a manual detour. Add a **Mining Laser** power-up: a rapid-firing laser that only ever targets asteroids and always fires at the nearest one, so the player can farm minerals passively while keeping their normal weapon trained on enemies.

## Users

- **Player (primary).** Wants minerals for the hold/reward loop without diverting aim from enemies.
- **Game/balance designer.** Wants one clean, data-driven power-up kind with tunable fire rate, damage and duration.

Example user stories:

- As a player, when I collect a Mining Laser my ship automatically fires rapid laser shots at the nearest asteroid, so I can farm minerals without stopping my attack on enemies.
- As a player, the Mining Laser never wastes shots on empty space or on enemies — it only fires at a live asteroid.
- As a player, when there are no asteroids, the Mining Laser is silent and does not distract me.

## Resolved decisions (producer answers)

- **D1 — Delivery model.** It is a **normal weapon power-up** that occupies one of the six loadout slots when permanently owned, and it has **upgrade levels** (the standard power-up level curve). It is an additive auxiliary weapon: collecting it does **not** replace the cannon, so the player can still damage enemies.
- **D2 — Acquisition & duration.** It is acquired as a **field pickup** (temporary level, reverts at its TTL, refreshable on re-collect) **and** as a **permanent hold-full reward** that stays owned in a slot and auto-fires for the rest of the run on a level-derived interval — mirroring the Orbital Strike precedent.
- **D3 — Targeting.** It targets the **nearest live asteroid of any size tier**, computed with wrapped distance so an asteroid just across the screen seam (including one currently off-screen) is a valid target. It **never** targets non-asteroid enemies. It retargets immediately to the new nearest asteroid when its current target is destroyed. When no live asteroid exists it fires nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new `mining_laser` power-up is present in `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` (`src/powerups/types.ts`) with a name, player-facing description, drop weight, temporary window and a level spec; it is a normal slot-occupying kind (not exempt at the six-slot cap) and has upgrade levels in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` + `src/data/powerup-levels.json`.
- Collecting a Mining Laser as a **field pickup** makes the ship auto-fire at the **nearest live asteroid** at a rapid beat-grid cadence for its temporary window; re-collecting refreshes the window and the level, and the level reverts to the permanent level (or unowned) when the window expires.
- Taking the **permanent hold-full reward** owns the Mining Laser in a slot and keeps it auto-firing at the nearest live asteroid for the rest of the run, on the level-derived cadence.
- Targeting uses **wrapped distance** so an asteroid across the screen seam (even off-screen) can be the nearest target; a nearer non-asteroid enemy is ignored in favour of an asteroid.
- The Mining Laser **never damages or targets non-asteroid enemies** (scouts, harvesters, boss, etc.).
- When no live asteroid exists, the Mining Laser fires **no shots** (no empty-space or forward-fallback fire).
- When the current target asteroid is destroyed, the Mining Laser retargets to the **new nearest** live asteroid on the next shot, including split children.
- The targeting rule is a pure, shared helper (asteroid-only nearest selection using wrapped distance) consumed by both the game and the gym, with gym↔game parity asserted by the existing duplicate-body/parity guards.
- The Mining Laser is exercised in the appropriate gym scene (mineral/asteroid gym and/or the combat power-up gym) and shares the same core code as `PlayScene`.
- A code-drawn drop icon, catalogue description and HUD/active-effect readout exist, and the drop pool, hold-full choice and gym help surfaces include the new kind consistently.
- Unit tests cover: target selection (only asteroids, nearest with wrap seam, idle when none, retarget on kill/child spawn), cadence/fire path, temporary-window expiry and permanent ownership, and gym↔game parity.
- Documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4 power-up table and count) and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, and any relevant wiki/docs entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Players can collect a Mining Laser that automatically chews through the nearest asteroids, making mineral farming passive so they can keep firing at enemies.

## Constraints

- Must not fork the power-up, effects, targeting, bullet or HUD seams — reuse the shared core so gym↔game parity holds by construction.
- Must not weaken the existing asteroid-skip rule for Arc/Orbital Strike (`src/utils/targetEligibility.ts`); the Mining Laser is the explicit, documented inverse.
- Must not target enemies, ever — even a nearer enemy must be ignored in favour of an asteroid.
- It is a slot-occupying power-up with upgrade levels, not a cannon-replacing weapon and not a timed hit-and-forget weapon drop.
- Tuning (fire cadence, damage, TTL, drop weight, level curve) is balance data recorded in the work item, not hard-coded behaviour spread across scenes.
- No frame-rate-dependent behaviour; cadence runs on the shared beat/onset grid.

## Existing state

- Power-ups are a 16-kind catalogue (`PowerUpId`) with a permanent/temporary level split, timed/instant windows, a shared `EffectsRegistry`, level specs in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` and data in `src/data/powerup-levels.json`; a run's loadout is capped at six permanent slots.
- Auto-firing power-ups already exist: the **Orbital Strike** (`strike`) fires a bolt at the nearest live **non-asteroid** enemy on a level-derived interval (`selectOrbitalStrikeTarget`, `src/scenes/core/strikeTargeting.ts`); the **Mystery UFO** spawns a drone that seeks the nearest mineral.
- Auto-targeting eligibility is centralised in the pure `src/utils/targetEligibility.ts` (`isEligibleAutoTarget` / `isInertWorldHazard`), which *excludes* the `asteroid` archetype for Arc and Orbital Strike.
- Asteroids are `src/entities/Asteroid.ts` (archetype `'asteroid'`, 1 HP, three tiers, four-edge screen wrap). Small-asteroid mineral drops are resolved by `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` / `asteroidKillDrops.ts`.
- The shared combat core (`src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`, `CombatScene.ts`) owns `_autoFire`, the beat clock and all power-up pulse/consumption steps; gym scenes inherit it.

## Desired change

Add a Mining Laser power-up kind whose auto-fire is an **asteroid-targeting** sibling of the Orbital Strike: a pure nearest-live-asteroid selector (wrapped distance, any tier), a shared core fire step that emits rapid laser shots at the target, permanent-slot and level-curve wiring, icon/HUD/drop wiring, and gym coverage — with the crystal-clear rule that it only ever fires at asteroids and is silent when none exist.

**Key Files:** (predicted)

- `src/powerups/types.ts` — add `'mining_laser'` to `PowerUpId` and a `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` entry (name, description, drop weight, `temporaryWindow`, slot-occupying/consumable flags as appropriate).
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` + `src/data/powerup-levels.json` — level spec (fire cadence, damage, temporary window, slot behaviour).
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — per-run/pending state and the consume/resolve seam for the shared combat core.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — shared `_updateMiningLaser` step (target → fire on cadence), consuming the level store.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — resolve a fired shot against the asteroid through the shared damage path.
- New pure helper (e.g. `src/scenes/core/miningLaserTargeting.ts` or an extension of `src/utils/targetEligibility.ts`) — nearest-live-asteroid selector using wrapped distance.
- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts` / `src/scenes/core/` bullet or hitscan seam — reuse the shared player-bullet path.
- `src/core/rules.ts` — default drop weight / drop-pool inclusion.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts`, `src/powerups/dropDescriptions.ts`, `src/powerups/slots.ts`, `src/ui/HUD.ts` — icon, description, slot integration, readout.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts` (and/or `GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`) — gym coverage and parity.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4), `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — documentation.
- Tests: `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `src/powerups/slots.*.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/*.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, `src/utils/targetEligibility.test.ts`, gym parity tests.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Target-selection edge cases.** Asteroids wrap at the screen seam; "nearest" must use wrapped distance (as `findNearestTarget` / `selectOrbitalStrikeTarget` do) so a target just across the seam — or off-screen across it — is chosen correctly.
- **Split chains.** Destroying a large/medium asteroid spawns children; the laser must retarget to a child (if still nearest) or another asteroid without firing into empty space.
- **Slot interaction.** It takes a permanent slot when owned and is not slot-cap-exempt; verify the hold-full choice gating and mini-boss wheel behave correctly at six owned slots.
- **Balance risk.** A rapidly auto-firing laser makes mineral farming near-passive; drop weight, cadence, damage and TTL should be tuned (start from Orbital Strike/Extra Life rarity precedents) and recorded.
- **Parity risk.** If any scene copies the fire logic instead of consuming the shared core, the duplicate-body guard/parity test will fail — implement once in the shared core.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Do **not** also add asteroid targeting to other weapons or add mining-laser variants; record such ideas as separate linked work items.

## Related work

- **Orbital Strike power-up (AH-0MVCRC1Q0007JAV1)** — nearest-target auto-firing power-up precedent (`strike`, `selectOrbitalStrikeTarget`, level-derived interval, field vs permanent).
- **Arc weapon should not affect asteroids (AH-0MVNSIG1O0049G69)** — the auto-target asteroid-skip rule the Mining Laser deliberately inverts.
- **Shared auto-target eligibility rule (AH-0MVVHAAUJ0080M9M / AH-0MVVHAD7Z005X5UW)** — `isEligibleAutoTarget` / `isInertWorldHazard`.
- **Asteroids drop collectable minerals (AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q)** and the shared mineral kill-drop helper (AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB) — the mineral economy the laser feeds.
- **Gym minerals / asteroid gym** (`src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts`) — natural observation scene.
- **Power-up catalogue + effects (epic AH-0MVCC8XSS007P01Z / AH-0MVCRC1Q0007JAV1)** — catalogue/level conventions.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Delivery model.** Should the Mining Laser fire **alongside** the player's normal weapon (player can still shoot enemies), or is it acceptable for it to **replace** the main weapon while active? Options: (a) auxiliary/additive; (b) cannon-replacing. — **Recommended:** (a) auxiliary — a cannon-replacing weapon that can only hit asteroids would leave the player unable to damage enemies. **Answer (producer):** "It's a normal weapon power up that takes one of the slots available, with upgrade levels." → Resolved as an **additive, slot-occupying power-up with upgrade levels** (does not replace the cannon). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — Acquisition & duration.** How should it be acquired? Options: (a) field pickup only, timed (~15 s) and refreshable; (b) field pickup **and** a permanent hold-full reward that repeats on a level-derived interval (Orbital Strike precedent); (c) permanent once collected. — **Recommended:** (b). **Answer (producer):** **B** — field pickup **and** permanent hold-full reward repeating on a level-derived interval. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — No-asteroid behaviour & asteroid tiers.** When no asteroid is present, should it be silent, and which asteroids are eligible? Options: (a) idle unless a live on-screen asteroid exists; target nearest any-tier asteroid; retarget on kill; (b) idle, but also consider off-screen asteroids across the wrap seam; (c) always fire forward when none exists. — **Recommended:** (a). **Answer (producer):** **B** — idle when none exists, but target the nearest live asteroid using **wrapped distance**, including asteroids across the screen seam / off-screen; nearest any-tier asteroid; retarget on kill. Source: interactive reply.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MV5CB6KO0079N08** – Remove the Power Pellet power-up from the game (completed)
- **AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6** – Design level curves for all power-ups (completed)
- **AH-0MVU3341U001B40T** – Orbital Strike must not target asteroids (producer rejection remediation) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mubvgi62004ed9q, 0muhmt5jc004wrsb, 0mvcc8xss007p01z, 0mvnsig1o0049g69, acceptance (+406 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mvcc8xss007p01z, acceptance, active, actual, add (+387 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mvcc8xss007p01z, 0mvnsig1o0049g69, acceptance, active, actual (+359 more)

## Plan (2026-11-09)

Decomposed into seven features, created in **test-first / dependency order**. Every phase is a vertical slice (code + tests + docs where the slice needs them), and each is a separate worktree/session.

| Phase | Feature | Depends on | Effort / risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Mining-laser target rule (asteroid-only, wrapped) — AH-0MW9QMMOT0014IU0 | — | S / Low |
| F2 | Mining-laser catalogue kind and level curve — AH-0MW9QMNYP006ZO6T | — | S / Medium |
| F3 | Shared core mining-laser fire step — AH-0MW9QMP2P0032BWW | F1, F2 | M / High |
| F4 | Mining-laser beam VFX and audio cue — AH-0MW9QMQ7B005WFH9 | F3 | S / Low |
| F5 | Mining-laser surfaces: icon, description, drop, HUD — AH-0MW9QMRC7007HVHQ | F2 | S / Medium |
| F6 | Gym coverage and parity for the mining laser — AH-0MW9QMSI7005UU9P | F3, F5 | M / Medium |
| F7 | Docs: GDD §4.4, balancing, GYM_PARITY and guards — AH-0MW9QMTWL0075S32 | F5, F6 | XS / Low |

Between phases the next item's description is re-read and updated with anything the previous phase learned (tuning values, helper names, VFX colour).

### Corrections to the predicted Key Files (facts, not intent)

- **`src/data/powerup-levels.json` does not exist.** The `src/data` parity JSONs are weapon-only (`weapon-levels.json`, `weapon-levels-parity.json`). Power-up level data lives solely in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, so the AC's "+ JSON" clause is satisfied by that module alone. No new JSON file is invented unless a separate parity-file capability is requested.
- **`src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts` is not the fire seam.** The laser resolves as an **instant beam** (see Recorded assumptions), so it reuses `CombatScene.damageEnemyViaAoe` (the shared kill seam) plus a new `src/vfx/miningLaserBeam.ts`, mirroring the `strike` precedent (`vfx/orbitalStrike.ts`). No change to the player-bullet path is needed.
- The targeting helper is `src/scenes/core/miningLaserTargeting.ts` (the first, not the second, predicted option) and reuses `findNearestTarget` + `wrappedDistance` rather than re-implementing nearest selection.

### Recorded assumptions (correctable at review, not blocking)

1. **Instant beam, not a travelling projectile.** A projectile can collide with a non-asteroid enemy in flight, which the "never damages enemies" AC forbids; an instant resolve damages only the selected asteroid. A hitscan beam also works in gyms whose formation config collects no bullets (`GymMinerals` has `collectBullets: () => []`).
2. **No latched/banked shots.** Unlike the Orbital Strike (which latches a decided bolt so a pickup is never wasted), a cadence tick with no asteroid is simply skipped — silence is the required behaviour, and there is no single consumable to waste.
3. **Provisional balance values** (all catalogue/level data, retunable without code): cadence base **4 sixteenth-note steps = 750 ms**, −1 step per level, floor **1 step = 187.5 ms**; damage **1 → 2** whole hits (inert today — every asteroid tier is 1 HP); field TTL **10 s** (weapon-window precedent); drop weight **2** (Orbital Strike / Smart Bomb rarity).
4. **Slot behaviour:** a normal slot-counted kind — not `availableWhenSlotsFull`, not `fieldPickupOnly`, not `consumable`; rewarded when owned (level-up offer + mini-boss wedge).
5. **Gym coverage uses both observation scenes:** `GymMinerals` (asteroids only, currently no drop layer → opt in with a mining-laser-only spawner) shows the laser cutting, splitting and paying minerals; `GymPowerUpsCombat` (scouts only) shows the silence rule.
6. **The fire step lives in the shared core** and is called from `_tickPlayer` beside `_updateOrbitalStrike`, so `PlayScene` and every gym run identical code (the duplicate-body guard enforces it).

### OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking — defaults above are recorded so implementation can proceed)

- **Balance sign-off (game/balance designer).** Are the provisional cadence (0.75 s → 0.1875 s), damage (1 → 2), field TTL (10 s) and drop weight (2) the intended starting point, or should the laser be rarer/slower because passive farming is strong? The values are data; changing them later is a one-file edit in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` + `src/core/rules.ts`.
- **Feel (producer).** Instant beam vs travelling laser bolts. The instant beam is chosen for the "never damages enemies" guarantee and is the shipped default; a bolt look would need an asteroid-only collision filter and a parity test.
- **Damage axis.** Keep `miningLaserDamage` even though every asteroid is 1 HP today (catalogue-consistency), or drop the axis and make cadence the only level curve?

### Appendix: clarifying questions & answers (continued)

- **Q4 — Level-data location.** The AC names `src/data/powerup-levels.json`; no such file exists and the `src/data` parity files are weapon-only. **Answer (agent, from repository inspection):** level data lives in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` only; the AC is satisfied there and no JSON is invented. Evidence: `ls src/data` (no powerup file), `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS`. Recorded as an AC-scope correction above.
- **Q5 — Fire delivery (beam vs projectile) for this codebase.** Auto-targeting offence's asteroid rule lives in `src/utils/targetEligibility.ts` (skip asteroids) and the strike's selector in `src/scenes/core/strikeTargeting.ts`. **Answer (agent, research):** add the explicit inverse predicate + a sibling selector that reuses `findNearestTarget(..., world)`; resolve fire instantly through `damageEnemyViaAoe`, matching the `strike` VFX seam (`src/vfx/orbitalStrike.ts`). Proposed to the producer as the non-blocking "feel" OPEN QUESTION above.
- **Q6 — Where can the behaviour be observed?** `GymMinerals` (`src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts`) is asteroids-only but has **no** field-drop layer; `GymPowerUpsCombat` cycles power-ups but fields scouts only. **Answer (agent, research):** opt `GymMinerals` into the existing shared `powerUps` layer config with a mining-laser-only spawner, and add the kind to the combat gym's cycle — both consume the shared core, no gym fork. Recorded as F6.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-09 — Initial decomposition (F1–F7) created, dependency edges wired (F3←F1,F2; F4←F3; F5←F2; F6←F3,F5; F7←F5,F6), predicted-Key-Files corrections and recorded balance assumptions appended, three non-blocking open questions recorded.

# Extra Life adaptive probabilities — Intake Brief (AH-0MW8178ZR0090CNY)

## Original request (verbatim)

> Create a minor increase in the probabiliyt of an extra life power up being dropped as the player loses lives. It should not be noticable, but the player should "feel lucky" when one drops and they are low on lives. This, presumably means the amount of increase is exponential as the player drops to only 1 life left. Also ensure that a mini-boss kill *always* leaves an extra life power up.

> **Producer answers received (this intake):** Q1 → **(a)** scale the
> `extra_life` weight in the existing weighted pool; Q2 → **(a)** always spawn
> a physical `extra_life` field pickup at the death position, in addition to the
> wheel reward, even at the life cap / full slots; Q3 → a **gentler curve than
> the offered (b): `1× / 2× / 4×` at `3 / 2 / 1` lives** (i.e. a multiplier of
> **`2^livesLost`**). Asteroid clarification: small asteroids **no longer drop
> lives** at shipped defaults — see "Existing state" below.

## Problem statement

Extra Life currently drops at one fixed rate for the whole run, regardless of
how many lives the player has left. A player down to their last life therefore
gets no extra recovery help, and the moment an Extra Life appears never feels
like a lucky break. Separately, defeating a bespoke mini-boss — the biggest
scheduled highlight of every level — never leaves a life on the field, so the
encounter has no guaranteed survivability payoff.

## Users

- **Players** — want a subtle, invisible-to-them safety net that makes an Extra
  Life feel like a lucky break exactly when they are low on lives, and want a
  mini-boss kill to reliably restore a life.
- **Designers / balance tuners** — need the adaptive curve and the mini-boss
  guarantee expressed as named, persisted tunables (not scattered magic
  numbers) so the feel can be retuned without code changes.
- **Developers / AI agents** — need the rule defined once in the shared core so
  the game and every gym cannot drift apart (gym↔game parity).

### Example user stories

- As a **player on my last life**, I want an Extra Life to drop a little more
  often than usual, so I get a genuine chance to turn a doomed run around —
  without ever noticing the game is helping me.
- As a **player who just beat a mini-boss**, I want the wreck to always leave
  an Extra Life, so the hardest fight in the level reliably pays back a life.
- As a **designer**, I want the adaptive curve in one tunable place so I can
  soften or sharpen the "lucky" feeling without touching gameplay code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Adaptive mechanism (one shared rule):** Extra Life drop
      propensity scales with the player's remaining lives by scaling the
      `extra_life` **weight inside the existing weighted per-kill drop pool**
      (the total per-kill drop chance is unchanged; Extra Life simply becomes a
      larger share of the drops that do occur). The multiplier is exactly
      `1×` at or above the run's starting lives and is monotonically
      non-decreasing as lives fall. The rule lives once in a shared pure helper
      consumed by both `PlayScene` and every drop-bearing gym.
- [ ] **AC2 — Curve is `1× / 2× / 4×` at `3 / 2 / 1` lives:** the multiplier is
      `2 ** livesLost`, where `livesLost = max(0, runStartingLives − lives)`
      (`runStartingLives` defaults to 3; a hangar deployment may override it).
      So `≥3` lives → `1×`, `2` lives → `2×`, `1` life → `4×` (and `3` lives
      per the formula). The multiplier is applied to the weight; because the
      weighted pool is normalised, the resulting *probability* uplift is
      slightly below the weight ratio — an intentional extra layer of
      subtlety. At 2 lives the increase is modest ("not noticeable"); at 1 life
      it is a clear but still small uplift.
- [ ] **AC3 — Statistically verifiable:** a seeded simulation (N ≥ 10 000
      representative kills per lives value, documented seed set) demonstrates
      that the Extra Life drop rate at 2 lives and 1 life strictly exceeds the
      full-lives baseline and follows the documented weight-multiplier curve
      within tolerance; the test does not depend on a single lucky seed.
- [ ] **AC4 — Mini-boss always drops one:** every mini-boss defeat spawns
      exactly one `extra_life` **field pickup** at/near the mini-boss death
      position, **in addition to** the existing spin-the-wheel reward, in
      `PlayScene` and `GymMiniBoss`. It spawns even at the 5-life cap and with a
      full slot pool; the normal drop separation nudge applies, and the existing
      six-slot collection gate and 5-life cap still govern pickup (a drop at the
      cap is simply not useful, but is still spawned).
- [ ] **AC5 — Tunables + persistence:** the curve constant (exponential base,
      default 2) and the starting-lives reference live in `GameRules` with
      documented defaults, clamped on load, and older rules blobs load
      unchanged. The adaptive multiplier composes with the existing level
      scaling (`powerUpDropChance` / `extraLifeDropChance`) and is applied after
      it, so the curve can never rise with campaign level.
- [ ] **AC6 — Parity & no duplicate implementation:** the rule exists once in a
      shared module and is consumed by the game and the gyms (including
      `GymMiniBoss` for the guaranteed drop); the repo-wide duplicate-body guard
      (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) passes.
- [ ] **AC7 — Tests:** unit tests cover the curve (`1×` at full lives,
      `2×` at 2, `4×` at 1, monotonic, clamping/guards), the mini-boss guarantee
      (exactly one `extra_life` spawned per defeat, game + gym), and the seeded
      distribution; the changed-scope test gate passes.
- [ ] **AC8 — Documentation:** the GDD §4.4 (Extra Life drop), §3.3.1 / §4.4.4
      (mini-boss defeat/reward — which today state the sweep is cosmetic and the
      wheel is the single reward), the game-rules documentation and code
      comments are updated, including any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Impact

A player who is down to their last life quietly sees Extra Life drops a little
more often — enough to feel lucky, never enough to notice — and every mini-boss
kill now reliably leaves one on the field.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity is mandatory** (`AGENTS.md`; `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`): the rule
  lives once in the shared core and is consumed by `PlayScene` and the relevant
  gym scenes (`GymFormationScene`, `GymMiniBoss`, and any asteroid/level gym
  that rolls Extra Life). No divergent copies.
- **Subtlety is a hard requirement:** the curve must not make Extra Life
  common; the player must not be able to perceive the manipulation.
- **No new art/assets:** reuse the existing `extra_life` code-drawn icon and
  shared drop pipeline.
- **Do not regress the deliberate supply reduction:** AH-0MW3MLTY3005MIXR /
  AH-0MW10ZVLH005IJRM halved the supply dial and turned the asteroid
  Extra-Life roll off. The adaptive uplift must be layered on top, not undo
  that tuning.
- **Extra Life stays field-pickup-only:** it must not leak back onto the
  hold-full choice or the mini-boss wheel (§4.4.4). The guaranteed mini-boss
  drop is a field pickup, not a wheel wedge.

## Existing state

- **Generic per-kill drop:** `PlayScene._maybeDropPowerUp()` rolls the
  level-resolved per-kill chance `powerUpDropChance(level, rules)` (0.09 at
  level 1 → 0.025 at level 10), then draws one kind from the shared weighted
  pool via `_drawNextDrop` (`src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts`,
  `CombatCoreScene._buildDefaultDropSpawner`). The spawner is built once at
  scene start with fixed weights; there is no per-kill weight adjustment today.
- **Extra Life weight:** fixed `DEFAULT_EXTRA_LIFE_WEIGHT = 3` in
  `src/core/rules.ts` (`defaultPowerUpWeights()`), against 4 for standard
  power-ups and 2 for the rare Smart Bomb / Orbital Strike. It never varies
  with lives.
- **Lives:** `GameState.lives` (start 3, cap `MAX_LIVES = 5` from the Extra
  Life catalogue entry). `Player`/HUD read the same value; the scene has
  `this.gameState.lives` at kill time.
- **Asteroid Extra Life roll — currently OFF:** `rollAsteroidExtraLife` +
  `extraLifeDropChance(level, rules)` in `src/scenes/core/asteroidKillDrops.ts`
  is **disabled at shipped defaults**
  (`DEFAULT_ASTEROID_EXTRA_LIFE_DROP_CHANCE = 0`, set by AH-0MW3MLTY3005MIXR /
  AH-0MW10ZVLH005IJRM). **So no, asteroids no longer drop lives.** The rule, the
  `asteroidExtraLifeDropChance` key and its clamping/persistence are retained
  so a designer can re-enable the roll with one config value; when they do, the
  adaptive multiplier defined here composes with it (at the default `0` there is
  no behaviour change).
- **Mini-boss defeat:** `PlayScene._damageMiniBoss` → `miniBoss.destroy()` runs
  the cosmetic death sweep (no drops, no score, no telemetry) and opens the
  spin-the-wheel reward (§4.4.4). Extra Life is deliberately excluded from the
  wheel. Consequently a mini-boss kill currently leaves **no** Extra Life.
- **Gym consumers:** `GymFormationScene` (`_rollExtraLifeDrop`), `GymLevel`,
  `GymMiniBoss` — the first two already call the shared asteroid roll; the
  mini-boss gym exercises the reward wheel.

## Desired change

1. Add a shared, pure **life-adaptive Extra Life weight multiplier**
   (`2 ** livesLost`, clipped to `≥ 1` and `1×` at/above the run's starting
   lives) and apply it to the `extra_life` weight in the shared weighted
   per-kill drop draw. At full lives the behaviour is byte-for-byte today's; at
   2 lives the likelihood doubles and at 1 life it quadruples, so the player
   "feels lucky" at 1 life without noticing at 2.
2. Make **every mini-boss defeat always spawn one `extra_life` field pickup**
   at/near the death position, on top of the wheel reward, in `PlayScene` and
   `GymMiniBoss`, regardless of the life cap or slot occupancy.
3. Express the curve as named, persisted `GameRules` tunables with documented
   defaults and load-time clamping.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/rules.ts` — add the adaptive-curve tunable (exponential base,
  default 2; starting-lives reference) to `GameRules`, defaults, clamping,
  schema-compatible load.
- `src/core/livesScaling.ts` **(new)** — the pure life→weight-multiplier helper
  (single source of truth), beside `levelScaling.ts`.
- `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts` / `CombatCoreScene.ts` — expose the
  Extra-Life weight adjustment through the shared drop draw so game + gyms
  share it (e.g. set the `extra_life` weight before each draw).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — apply the multiplier at kill time
  (`_maybeDropPowerUp`) and spawn the guaranteed Extra Life on mini-boss defeat
  (`_damageMiniBoss` / `_finaliseMiniBossDefeat`).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — consume the shared multiplier
  (full-lives baseline in a gym with no run).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMiniBoss.ts` — consume the guaranteed mini-boss drop
  (gym has no run lives: unconditional, matching the game's "always").
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/core/livesScaling.test.ts` **(new)**,
  `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.miniboss*.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — coverage.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4 / §3.3.1 / §4.4.4 wording.

## Related work

- **Add an extra life power up (AH-0MT7UX8LE0072MR3)** — introduced P8 Extra
  Life (passive +1, cap 5, rarer than standard drops). Completed.
- **Asteroids drop more lives (AH-0MV6M2M9P0078N4S)** — added the small-asteroid
  Extra-Life roll (`rollAsteroidExtraLife`, `asteroidExtraLifeDropChance`),
  later turned off by AH-0MW10ZVLH005IJRM. Completed.
- **Use level-resolved power-up drop chance in PlayScene
  (AH-0MVLJF5P0005KF8X)** — wired `powerUpDropChance` / `extraLifeDropChance`
  into the kill path. Completed.
- **Level-scaling curves (AH-0MVLJEE7O008RX9X)** — `src/core/levelScaling.ts`,
  the supply dial this feature composes with.
- **Supply-dial reduction / asteroid roll off (AH-0MW3MLTY3005MIXR,
  AH-0MW10ZVLH005IJRM)** — deliberate supply tightening; do not undo.
- **Mini-boss defeat sweep (AH-0MVOFGB6K003YD0Z)** — cosmetic sweep, no drops.
- **Mini-Boss Reward — Spin the Wheel (AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD)** — the encounter's
  current single reward; Extra Life is field-pickup-only and excluded from the
  wheel. The guaranteed drop in this item must not change that exclusion.
- **Bot prioritises extra lives (AH-0MV03GXZQ00801T4)** — the demo brain already
  prefers a live Extra Life pickup below the cap; unaffected but retested.
- **Duplicate check:** no completed item satisfies this brief's ACs. The
  closest completed items (above) implement fixed-rate Extra Life drops and the
  mini-boss reward; neither adapts the rate to lives nor guarantees a
  mini-boss Extra Life. No duplicate found.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Perceptibility risk (highest):** a curve tuned too high is noticeable and
  undermines the "not noticeable" requirement. The chosen `1×/2×/4×` curve is
  deliberately gentle; verify with a seeded statistical test and keep the base
  in `GameRules` for retuning.
- **Compounding with level scaling:** the supply dial already lowers drop
  chance with campaign level. The adaptive multiplier is applied after level
  scaling so a late-campaign player on 1 life still gets the intended uplift.
- **Weight vs probability:** the multiplier scales the *weight*, so the
  resulting probability uplift is slightly below the weight ratio because the
  pool normalises. This is intentional subtlety; the statistical test asserts
  the resulting *probability* ordering, not just the weight.
- **Mini-boss drop at the cap:** a guaranteed drop at 5 lives or with a full
  slot pool may be useless. Producer answer Q2(a): **still spawn it** —
  "always" is literal; the six-slot gate and life cap handle collection.
- **Gym semantics:** gyms have no run lives. `GymMiniBoss` always spawns the
  guaranteed drop; the adaptive multiplier uses the catalogue starting lives
  (3) as the baseline in gyms, so parity tests are deterministic.
- **Asteroid roll is off:** the multiplier's composition with the asteroid roll
  has no visible effect at the shipped default (`0`); it is defined for
  consistency if a designer re-enables the roll.
- **Scope-creep risk:** do not add a HUD "pity counter", a visible luck meter,
  or extra-life bounties here — record any such idea as a linked work item.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Which drop channel should adapt? (mechanism)**
  - (a) Scale the `extra_life` **weight inside the existing weighted per-kill
    pool** (drop frequency unchanged; Extra Life becomes a larger share of the
    existing drops as lives fall).
  - (b) Add a separate independent Extra Life roll per kill.
  - (c) Raise the overall per-kill drop chance when low on lives.
  - **Answer (producer): (a).** Source: interactive reply.

- **Q2 — What does "mini-boss kill always leaves an extra life power up" mean
  exactly?**
  - (a) Always spawn a physical `extra_life` **field pickup** at the death
    position, in addition to the wheel reward, even at the cap / full slots.
  - (b) Same, but only when below the life cap.
  - (c) Add Extra Life as a wheel wedge/outcome instead of a field pickup.
  - **Answer (producer): (a).** Source: interactive reply.

- **Q3 — Curve shape, magnitude, and interaction with level scaling.**
  - (a) `multiplier = base ** livesLost` (base ≈ 2.5–3 offered).
  - (b) A gentler/other curve or a per-lives table (e.g. `1× / 2× / 5×`).
  - (c) Also compose the multiplier into the asteroid Extra-Life roll.
  - **Answer (producer): an even gentler curve than (b) — `1× / 2× / 4×` at
    `3 / 2 / 1` lives.** This is exactly `multiplier = 2 ** livesLost`. For
    (c), the producer's follow-up question ("Asteroids no longer drop lives, do
    they?") was answered: the asteroid Extra-Life roll is **off at shipped
    defaults** (`0`), so there is no live asteroid source today; the shared
    multiplier is nonetheless defined once and applied to every Extra Life
    source so it composes if the roll is re-enabled (no behaviour change at
    `0`). Source: interactive reply + repository inspection
    (`src/core/rules.ts:341`, `src/scenes/core/asteroidKillDrops.ts`).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVLJF5P0005KF8X** – Use level-resolved power-up drop chance in PlayScene (completed)
- **AH-0MV03GXZQ00801T4** – Bot prioritises extra lives in hold-full choice and on-screen pickups (completed)
- **AH-0MT7UX8LE0072MR3** – Add an extra life power up (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mv03gxzq00801t4, 0mv6m2m9p0078n4s, 0mvlisu03006wdod, 0mvofgb6k003yd0z, 0mw10zvlh005ijrm (+499 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mv6m2m9p0078n4s, 0mw10zvlh005ijrm, able, ac1, ac2 (+469 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mv6m2m9p0078n4s, 0mvofgb6k003yd0z, 0mw10zvlh005ijrm, able, ac1 (+427 more)

# Add regression tests for pulse-wave lifecycle and constant-stroke render

## Problem

No automated tests cover the pulse-wave lifecycle: supersede, range exit, boss destroy, or constant-stroke render policy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- At least one new or extended automated test covers the wave lifecycle (supersede, range exit, boss destroy) and the constant-stroke render path.
- Supersede test: fire two volleys inside one wave lifetime; assert exactly one wave sprite in the display list.
- Range exit test: let a wave reach the edge of the screen; assert zero wave sprites in the display list.
- Boss destroy test: destroy the boss; assert zero wave sprites remain.
- Constant-stroke test: assert that the wave Graphics object uses a constant line width regardless of radius.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Key Files

- src/entities/Boss.test.ts — new or extended tests for wave lifecycle.

data.description:
Part of `Review ring 2 aggression floor against the measured builds/losses split (AH-0MVWWGN92008P366)` — carries the producer's Q1 = (a) tune and Q2 = (c) broad band decision.

# Goal

As a player who has just secured ring 1, I want ring 2's weaker hexes to be beatable on the first attempt with my ring-1 loadout, so the ring's authored aggression spread reads as a difficulty gradient instead of twelve identical losses.

# Target outcome

Ring 2's six weakest hexes (the ones authored at aggression 3–4) move to **aggression 2** — campaign level 3, the last no-fire level of `difficulty-curves.csv` and the band the competent bot survived at full 300 s on ring 1 — while the hard tail keeps its gradient: four hexes at 5, one at 6, and the weapon hex `hex-r2-12` at 8 as ring 2's strict maximum.

Resulting authored ring-2 aggressions (`hex-r2-1` … `hex-r2-12`):

`2, 2, 5, 2, 5, 2, 2, 5, 6, 2, 5, 8`

so `hex-r2-1`, `hex-r2-2`, `hex-r2-4`, `hex-r2-6`, `hex-r2-7`, `hex-r2-10` move 3/4 → 2; `hex-r2-3`, `hex-r2-5`, `hex-r2-8`, `hex-r2-11` stay 5; `hex-r2-9` stays 6; `hex-r2-12` stays 8.

This is the parent's "broad band" shape. Its arithmetic projects **≈98.1 min** (95.4–102.2) — in-window against the restored 70–100 window — with **6 of 12** first attempts captured (up from 0 of 12) and the modelled retry allowance halving from 60 to 30 min. Every minute figure there is a projection from the committed baseline; the authoritative values come from `npm run ring-timing` in `Restore ring 2's 70–100 window and regenerate the ring-timing evidence`.

# Definition of done

- Both authored data sources carry the new numbers and stay in parity.
- The band, floor and retained gradient are pinned by tests written before the data edit.
- The two consumers that encode ring 2's weakest hex (attract bot, map focus) are updated with a stated reason rather than silently re-pinned.
- Changed-scope tests green, including the ring-definition validation and the ring-timing arena tests. The retuned ring-2 grind mean also lands inside the currently committed 90–120 window, so this item is green on its own.

# Constraints

- **Authoring, not a new difficulty system.** Aggression → campaign level stays `hexAggressionLevel` in `src/core/hangarWar/hexDifficulty.ts`; no parallel scaling path.
- **Ring rules are pinned by tests:** exactly one weapon hex per ring, it is the ring's strict maximum, ring 2's floor stays above ring 1's floor and ring 2's maximum above ring 1's.
- **Data parity:** `src/data/hex-ring-2.csv` and `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` are edited together; a parity test fails if they drift.
- **Keep the gradient.** The 5s, the 6 and the weapon hex stay in the ring — do not drop the hard tail into the survivable band (parent risk "flattening the frontier").
- **No harness rework and no window change here.** `RING_TIMING_TARGETS`, the budget assertion and the docs are the sibling item's scope (Q3 scope-creep guard).

# Risky assumptions

- Level-3 survival reproduces on ring 2's level-3 hexes as it did on ring 1's (full 300 s in all three seeds). If a level-3 run does not survive on some seed, the captured count is measured in the sibling item and the band is re-examined there.
- Lowering aggression also lowers `hexBossHpMultiplier` (1.18 → 1.12 at aggression 2) and the frontier tick's attack force for those hexes. Both are intended consequences of authoring, not regressions.

# Key Files

- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` — the `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` ring-2 rows (runtime source of truth).
- `src/data/hex-ring-2.csv` — the seed mirror (parity).
- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.test.ts` — the ring-rule pins plus the new band pins.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.test.ts` — the attract bot's weakest-hex expectations.
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts` — the default map focus expectation.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDifficulty.ts` — the unchanged aggression → level mapping (referenced).

# Acceptance Criteria

- `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` ring-2 `baseAggression` values are `2, 2, 5, 2, 5, 2, 2, 5, 6, 2, 5, 8` for `hex-r2-1` … `hex-r2-12`, `src/data/hex-ring-2.csv` mirrors them byte-for-value, and the CSV↔table parity test is green.
- A new test in `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.test.ts` pins ring 2's floor at aggression 2, every hex at aggression ≤ 2 resolving through `hexAggressionLevel` to campaign level ≤ 3 (the survivable band), the retained gradient (a hex at 5 and a hex at 6 remaining), and the weapon hex `hex-r2-12` as ring 2's strict maximum at 8.
- The ring-definition validation still holds: exactly one weapon hex per ring and it is ring 2's strict maximum, ring 2's floor stays above ring 1's floor and ring 2's maximum above ring 1's maximum, so `validateRingDefinitions(2, …)` reports ok.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.test.ts` and `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts` are updated for the retuned data: `pickAttractHex` now resolves ring 2's joint-weakest tie to `hex-r2-1` (fresh ring and default map focus), and the adjacency test still discriminates adjacency from raw weakness by lowering a non-adjacent hex's aggression — each restated assertion carries a comment stating why the expected id is the one it is.
- The changed-scope test gate (`/skill:test`) passes, covering `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.test.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.test.ts`, `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts` and `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts`.
